sahneler.metin: Part of the core at Three Mile Island melted down.
Cooling water escaped for hours through a valve stuck open.
Their panel light said the valve was closed.
It only showed the close signal was sent, not the valve's position.
Thinking there was too much water, they cut emergency cooling.
The core overheated and partly melted.
That's why control rooms and training were rebuilt afterward.

Three Mile Island partially melted down. The cause: loss of coolant through a stuck-open pilot-operated relief valve, misread by operators.
